nodes.name: Hydrothermal NiFe precursor synthesis
nodes.procedure: Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (x mmol), Fe(NO3)3·9H2O (1-x mmol), and CO(NH2)2 (10 mmol) were dissolved in 36 mL of distilled water and stirred to form a transparent and homogeneous solution. And then, the aqueous solution and the Ni foam were transferred to a 40 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave, which was sealed, maintained at 120°C for 12 h, and then allowed to cool to room temperature naturally. The NiFe precursor was taken out and washed with water thoroughly before being dried at 80°C for 6 h.

nodes.name: Phosphorization of NiFe precursor
nodes.procedure: To prepare (NixFe1-x)2P nanosheet arrays, NiFe precursor and 110 mg NaH2PO2 were put in a porcelain boat. Subsequently, the samples were heated at 300°C for 2 h in a flow Ar atmosphere.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show Ni₀.₃₃Fe₀.₆₇ precursor nanosheet arrays ≈15 nm thick with smooth surface and (Ni₀.₃₃Fe₀.₆₇)₂P nanosheet arrays maintaining morphology with increased surface roughness.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images (Figure 1A and Figure S1A (Supporting Information)) showed that the Ni₀.₃₃Fe₀.₆₇ precursor nanosheet arrays with a thickness of ≈15 nm and smooth surface densely grew on the Ni foam.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns for (NiₓFe₁₋ₓ)₂P (x > 0) nanosheet arrays match well with Ni₂P phase structure (JCPDS no. 03-0953).
nodes.evidence_snippet: A series of peak diffraction of X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns for (NiₓFe₁₋ₓ)₂P (x > 0) nanosheet arrays matched well with Ni₂P phase structure (JCPDS no. 03-0953, Figure S4A, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping reveals uniform distribution of Fe, Ni, and P elements; atomic ratio Ni:Fe = 2.15:1 for (Ni₀.₃₃Fe₀.₆₇)₂P.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The element mapping results revealed the existence of Fe with uniform distribution as well as Ni and P elements and illustrated the successful transformation from NiFe precursor to Fe uniformly doped Ni₂P nanosheet arrays.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS P 2p spectrum shows peaks at 134.4 eV (oxidized metal phosphate) and 129.2 eV (metal phosphides); Ni 2p peaks at 853.0 eV (Ni in Fe-doped Ni₂P) and 856.1 eV (Ni oxide); Fe 2p shows Fe²⁺ (711.5/723.6 eV) and Fe³⁺ (715.6/727.3 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution P 2p spectrum shows two main peaks at 134.4 and 129.2 eV (Figure 1F). The peak at 129.2 eV is corresponding to metal phosphides and the other peak at 134.4 eV reflects the oxidized metal phosphate species.
